creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Updating this Mac from main means waiting about 45 minutes for the release path (CI gate, then notarization), though notarization only matters for a copy another Mac downloads. Done by hand on 2026-10-11, 0.13.0 to 0.15.0:

```sh
MUSTER_INSTALL=release \
MUSTER_SIGN_IDENTITY="Developer ID Application: Alexander Terp (CV4835A2BN)" \
./dev --bundle
# quit Muster, replace /Applications/Muster.app with .build/muster.app, reopen it with env -i
```

Both settings matter. `MUSTER_INSTALL=release` names the daemon's socket, so the new app takes over the release daemon's panes rather than starting a second daemon. The Developer ID keeps macOS permissions: TCC keys a Developer ID grant to team and bundle id, but an ad-hoc build's to its cdhash, which changes every build. All five panes and Full Disk Access survived the swap.

A command could do the build and the swap, refusing when the keychain holds no Developer ID, since an ad-hoc build in /Applications silently drops every permission. Open questions: a `./dev` flag or a script of its own like `./release` (`./dev` builds and checks a tree); whether it refuses a dirty tree; and what it says about Homebrew's record, which keeps naming the version brew installed, so a later `brew upgrade` or Upgrade muster replaces the local build with the release - which is also the way back.
title: Install a Developer ID-signed build of this tree into /Applications in one command
